title: Betrayed by Boomers
summary: A cultural rant against the gym 'boomer', defined as a mindset rather than an age: out-of-shape men who brag about unverifiable past lifts and spread 'age cope', the idea that the male body falls apart from your 20s. NH argues that testosterone stays fairly stable from 20 to 50, that muscle comes from years of exposure rather than the puberty peak, and that boomers have left young men without role models. He ends on a dark reflection about old age as a slow sinking ship.
claims: A 'boomer' in the gym is a mindset, not an age: you can be one at 26 and a 70-year-old can be a fine example
Gym boomers approach people unprompted to brag about what they used to lift; people who are actually in shape never need to do this because their body shows it
Unverifiable claims of past lifts should be ignored: pics or it didn't happen
A stranger once told him he had squatted 1200 lb barefoot and unequipped, which would have beaten the world record by about 400 lb
He has seen exactly one person bench 500 lb in person in his whole life
Most of gym culture is people pushing others down because they feel bad about themselves; confident people help others
Respect is earned through actions and experience, not owed because of age
'Age cope', the belief that the body inevitably breaks down with age, is a lie that lets people dodge responsibility for their lifestyle
The age at which people say the body starts declining keeps getting younger: it was 50, then 40, then 30, and now he hears people say after 25 it's all downhill
The puberty testosterone peak lasts about 3 years; the much longer stable period afterwards matters more for muscle because muscle is built by cumulative exposure over time, not peaks
Steroid users do not get huge from one cycle; they get big from years of constant high hormone levels, which shows it is the duration that builds mass
Testosterone stays fairly stable from your 20s to your 50s with only a slow decline, and some men see higher levels in their 30s or 40s
Most muscle is built after puberty, between your 20s and 50s, not during adolescence
Low testosterone and bad bodies in older men usually come from years of inactivity, not from age itself
'Squats are bad for your knees' is a boomer myth; knee pain comes from being fat and inactive and squatting with bad form
Men in their 30s do not need TRT; teens and young men going on TRT will shut down their own production and become what they feared
At a party of 15 men in their early 30s, only two were in shape: him and an army guy
The 'dad bod' is a harmful excuse; fathers should be at their strongest to set an example for their children
Most fitness YouTubers he respects are around his age because the older generation failed to provide good role models
He helped an old man off a bus in Paris who tearfully said he used to squat 200 kg; nostalgia for lost strength is understandable when it isn't used to put others down
A rich man in his 50s set a safety clip on a boat rope and told teenage NH to pull it so he would fail; NH broke the clip by brute strength and the man was furious
We all age but we don't have to get old: staying active keeps you young in spirit and body
He says Arnold became a sellout politician and is now a 'corpse' of who he used to be
